## Packages

The package list is the one used for the published analysis:

-   **Data import and management:** [{readxl}](https://readxl.tidyverse.org/) reads the Excel workbook; [{tidyverse}](https://www.tidyverse.org/) (including [{stringr}](https://stringr.tidyverse.org/)) handles cleaning and reshaping [@wickham2019tidyverse]; [{haven}](https://haven.tidyverse.org/) supplies `as_factor()`, used to turn categorical variables into factors.
-   **Tables:** [{gtsummary}](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/) builds Table 1 and the regression tables [@sjoberg2021gtsummary]; [{bstfun}](https://github.com/MSKCC-Epi-Bio/bstfun) adds the inline forest plots to those tables; [{flextable}](https://davidgohel.github.io/flextable/) formats the PCA eigenvalue table.
-   **Figures:** [{ggplot2}](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/), [{ggbeeswarm}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggbeeswarm) (quasirandom points) and [{ggpubr}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggpubr) (Wilcoxon p-values on the plot); [{corrplot}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=corrplot) for correlation matrices.
-   **Modeling:** [{broom}](https://broom.tidymodels.org/) (attached, but not called directly by the scripts); [{pROC}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pROC) for ROC curves and AUC confidence intervals [@robin2011proc]; [{cutpointr}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=cutpointr) for optimal titer cutpoints [@thiele2021cutpointr]; [{factoextra}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=factoextra) for PCA eigenvalues and plots.

{bstfun} is not on CRAN; install it from GitHub with `remotes::install_github("MSKCC-Epi-Bio/bstfun")`.

## Constants

The study workbook is restricted and never committed. `raw_data_path` points to the authorized local copy, which by default sits in `data-raw/`, a folder excluded by `.gitignore`. Only the sheet named `Data` is used. The scripts write their outputs to `tables/` and `figures/`.

```{r}
#| label: define-constants
#| eval: false
```

## Display labels

Readable names for variables and category codes, used only when tables are saved (for example `RACE` with codes `W`/`B` becomes "Race: White/Black", and `DrugMycophenolate` `TRUE`/`FALSE` becomes "Mycophenolate: Yes/No"). The analysis itself keeps the original variable names; see `relabel_table()` in [Functions](functions.qmd).
